_doc: Inventory of upstream source documents mirrored into the repository, and
therefore redistributed in every checkout and every deployed build.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The corpus licence machinery (NVDM envelopes, the
Headwaters registry, nvdm-encumbrance-report.py, sample-corpus.json) only
ever looked at public/data and public/geojson. public/docs was invisible to
all of it, so a 4.4 MB mirror of CPCB's Polluted River Stretches report
shipped in every checkout while the registry entry for its own source said
the publisher requires approval for any use beyond download and print.
Removing that one file fixed the instance; this manifest plus
scripts/check-mirrored-documents.py fixes the shape, by making every
mirrored document name its source and be gated on that source's terms.
THE RULE, and it is an ALLOWLIST. A mirror ships only on an AFFIRMATIVE
right to redistribute the whole document, by exactly one of three routes:
1. `permission`           - an actual grant, recording grantor,
granted_on and form.
2. `redistribution_basis` - a quoted clause that permits redistribution,
with source_url and verified_on.
3. source classifies      - a canonical open grant (CC BY, CC0, GODL,
`clean-open`             ODC-BY and friends).
Every other state fails, and the checker enumerates them rather than
denying them one at a time: gov-attribution is a description of our
CITATION practice, not a licence to republish a PDF; share-alike permits
redistribution only on terms a file drop does not offer; nc, third-party,
vague, restricted and UNCLASSIFIED all obviously fail. A `status` field is
documentation and is never a route on its own - that was the bug in the
first version of this gate, which failed only on 'restricted' and let six
documents with explicitly unproven rights through on a printed warning.
Mirroring is redistribution. Extracted factual VALUES are a different
question and are unaffected - facts carry no copyright - which is why
deleting a mirror never means dropping the numbers derived from it.
`documents` is the live inventory and is what the gate checks. `removed`
is the audit trail: documents that were mirrored here, could not be
cleared, and are now cited at the publisher instead. Keep the record - the
next person to consider mirroring one of these should find out why it
went, rather than re-adding it.

removed.reason: cpcb.gov.in/copyright-policy/ permits material to be downloaded to file or printer and makes 'Any other proposed use of the material is subject to the approval of competent authority of CPCB'. Mirroring is redistribution and no approval was ever sought, so the mirror had no basis. The BOD-band Priority I-V values extracted from it stay: facts carry no copyright.

KSPCB's own copyright policy page was not retrievable on 2026-07-31 (the Karnataka government template URL 404s), so nothing affirmatively permits redistribution. The Karnataka Open Data Policy 2021 is a further unresolved question over every Karnataka state source. Action plans filed before the NGT may well be tabled documents, which would be a stronger and quite different basis - but that has not been established, and an unestablished basis is not a basis.

Memo PCB/150/Infra/2025, obtained as an RTI response via Paani Earth. An RTI response is supplied to the requester; that it reached us is not a grant to republish it, and it has no public upstream URL to point at. Removed rather than guessed about.

BWSSB's copyright policy page (read 2026-07-31) prints BOTH Karnataka government templates side by side - one permitting republication in any format free of charge with attribution, one requiring prior authorisation - without saying which governs. Two contradictory templates are not a grant. BWSSB is also a public undertaking owning its copyright independently under Copyright Act s.17(dd), so the OpenCity CKAN label on a sibling dataset never reached this PDF.
